summary.title: Building a JIRA integration with Clojure & Atlassian Connect
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a Clojure web app that registers with JIRA via Atlassian Connect, receives webhook events on issue changes, stores them, and shows a live activity feed in a ClojureScript/React front end.
takeaways: Atlassian Connect works by publishing a JSON descriptor (connect.json) that lists the app's base URL, modules, webhooks and scopes, which JIRA loads.
JIRA sends webhook events (e.g. jira:issue_updated) to a POST endpoint, which can be parsed and stored; the demo uses an in-memory atom.
ngrok can expose a local Clojure server over HTTPS so JIRA Cloud can reach it during development.
A ClojureScript front end using Rum (React) and cljs-ajax can poll the server every 5 seconds to show a live issue feed.
summary.summary: The article walks through building a small JIRA integration in Clojure using Leiningen, Compojure and Ring, with the clj-connect library for Atlassian Connect. It covers serving a Connect descriptor, handling the /installed lifecycle callback, exposing a webhook endpoint that transforms and stores issue events, and testing over an ngrok HTTPS tunnel. The second half adds a ClojureScript UI built with Figwheel, Rum and AJAX polling to display the activity feed. The author notes that the demo omits JWT validation and real persistence, and the full source is on GitHub.
